name: Samsung SDS Cloud Platform

modes.label: Virtual Server, no contract (hourly, open-source OS)
modes.note: Official USD list prices (USD/hour, "All prices exclude VAT", "Without Contract (USD/hour)") from the service portal price data (cloud.samsungsds.com/serviceportal/assets/js/data/price/virtualServerPrice.js, rendered at serviceportal/pricing.html?item=VS&product=compute), region KR_WEST (identical in KR_WEST_2), Open-source OS column. Sizes: 1st Gen (Ice Lake), 2nd Gen (Sapphire Rapids), 3rd Gen (Granite Rapids) standard Virtual Servers, 1-16 vCore. e.g. 4 vCore / 8 GB: $0.2191 (1st), $0.193 (2nd), $0.2052 (3rd). Billing unit/rounding not stated beyond "Charge by used hour"; granularity left null. "* 1 month (730 hours) is applied for usage without contract."

modes.label: Planned Compute 1 year
modes.note: Planned Compute 1-year (instance-type commitment), official USD list, KR_WEST (=KR_WEST_2), Open-source OS, VAT excluded. Fixed monthly fee per committed instance type; sizes.hour = monthly/730. Early cancellation penalty = monthly fee x 50% x remaining months. Discount vs on-demand is ~35% (1y) / ~40% (3y) for standard types, not the headline 'up to 55%'. Cost Savings (hourly spend commitment) gives near-identical hourly rates (s2v4m8: $0.1252 1y / $0.1157 3y).

modes.label: Virtual Server, no contract, Windows
modes.note: Official USD list, KR_WEST, Windows column (licence included), VAT excluded.

modes.label: Accelerated Server (GPU/NPU), no contract
modes.note: Official USD list, KR_WEST, Ubuntu (open source) column, VAT excluded. 'Even when a server is stopped, the usage fee is charged the same.' RNGD is a FuriosaAI NPU.

modes.label: Accelerated Server (GPU/NPU) Spot
modes.note: Spot, no contract only; no SLA, may be reclaimed at any time.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Pay-per-use: "only charging for usage" / "Charge by used hour" (pricing page); no platform fee published. Quotas unknown, not confirmed unlimited.

caveats: On-demand rates: official USD list (KR_WEST = KR_WEST_2 'Enterprises/Finance' offering), Open-source OS column, excluding VAT (verified 2026-09-29). USD list = KRW/1150. Sovereign (KR_SOUTH) offering is KRW-only and ~20% higher; not modelled.
Billing: 'Charge by used hour'; no-contract VMs bill only while on (FAQ: no server fee when turned off, excluding GPU). Sub-hour granularity/minimum is not published; granularity left null.
Boot disk is not included: OS disk is a Block Storage volume (min 16 GB Linux) at $0.1043/GB-month SSD, billed monthly on allocation even when the VM is stopped.
Public IPv4 $0.00487/h (~$3.56/month) billed while reserved; internet egress first 20 GB/month free then $0.087/GB.
Planned Compute / Cost Savings: ~35% (1y) / ~40% (3y) off standard VMs for a fixed monthly commitment with a 50% early-cancellation penalty; headline 'up to 55%' is not typical for VMs.
Sign-up: console account + payment method; trial credit USD 260 once, valid 3 months. Default quotas not published (Quota Service, some auto-approved).

fleet.notes: Official Quota Service describes account/region resource limits and console increase requests; some auto-approve, others are not promised automatic. No public numeric fresh-account Virtual Server/vCPU/GPU limit, verification details or SLA established. Max 5 VPCs per account (FAQ); a Memory quota item was added on 2026-09-15.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.note: Plain KVM-style VM: stopping a Virtual Server just powers it off (Block Storage OS disk persists). No state capture on stop. Scheduled snapshots exist for File Storage ('immediate or scheduled snapshot creation', retention count) and the Backup service runs scheduled VM-image backups (daily/weekly/monthly) - both scheduled, not on stop.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Image creation: You can create an Image from the configuration of the Virtual Server you are using, and you can also create an Image by uploading your Image file to Object Storage.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk only, no memory. 'Snapshot-Based' Images of a VM can boot new Virtual Servers and be shared with other accounts (docs recommend stopping the server first for FS consistency). Block Storage volumes also have on-demand snapshots: restore in place or 'Create recovery volume' as a new volume; snapshots billed on source volume size. Console/API/CLI (API and CLI references exist).

harness_api.note: General-purpose IaaS VM; no agent/harness API in the Virtual Server guide or product pages.

egress_allowlist.quote: When a Security Group is first created, it blocks all inbound and outbound traffic according to the default rule (Any/Deny).
egress_allowlist.note: Security Group outbound allow rules by target IP/CIDR, protocol, port; plus per-VPC Internet Gateway Firewall (also default Any Deny, IP/port/protocol rules). No FQDN rules documented.

ingress_rules.quote: Users can specify an IP address, port, and protocol to create inbound/outbound rules, and only traffic allowed by the created rules can access the target resources.
ingress_rules.note: Security Groups (default deny) plus IGW/Load Balancer firewalls; public NAT IP is opt-in.

guest_firewall.note: Full VM (Linux/Windows images) with root/Administrator via key pair; iptables/nftables/Windows Firewall work inside.

secret_proxy.quote: Remove hardcoding of sensitive information in application source code and retrieve it by calling Secrets stored securely in a Key-Value format.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets Manager / Secret Vault are KMS-encrypted secret stores the workload reads; no credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.note: Block Storage data volumes 8 GB-12 TB, SSD/HDD, online expansion; up to 26 volumes per Virtual Server.

volume_shared.quote: File Storage allows servers connected via the network to easily store and share data, making it a storage solution suitable for application environments that use multiple servers.
volume_shared.note: File Storage over NFS (Linux) or CIFS (Windows), read-write, auto-scaling capacity. Block Storage SSD/HDD_MultiAttach volumes also attach to 2+ Virtual Servers at once ('no limit on the number of servers per volume'; not for Windows).
